title: Noise & Hearing Protection
whatItIs: Loud noise can permanently damage hearing and cause tinnitus. The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 set action values and limits for daily exposure.

keyFacts.text: From 80 dB(A) a day, employers MUST assess the risk and give hearing protection to anyone who asks.
From 85 dB(A), employers MUST reduce noise, provide protectors and set Hearing Protection Zones.
Exposure MUST NOT go above 87 dB(A), counting any hearing protection worn.
Workers MUST use the hearing protection provided and report any defects in it.

keyFacts: If you must raise your voice to talk to someone about 2 m away, noise is a problem.
Hearing protection doesn't replace cutting noise at source: it can fail or be misused.

onTheTest.question: What is the upper exposure action value for daily noise exposure?
onTheTest.why: Noise Regulations reg 4: lower action value 80 dB(A), upper action value 85 dB(A), exposure limit 87 dB(A).

onTheTest.question: An area of the site is marked as a Hearing Protection Zone. What must you do?
options: Wear it only if the noise hurts
Take it off when you need to talk
Wear hearing protection before you go in
onTheTest.why: Reg 7(3): no one should enter a Hearing Protection Zone without protectors. Reg 8(2): use them properly.

traps: Noise damage is permanent: lost hearing doesn't come back.
Ear protection is not the first control: noise must be reduced at source first.
Too much protection is risky too: you still need to hear warnings.
Protectors only work if worn the whole time and fitted properly.
